newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prosecutors question DKB on 'sokaiya' loans--NHK.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors question DKB on 'sokaiya' loans--NHK.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors have begun questioning exectives of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) over loans to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer, the NHK public television reported on Thursday.
The report said bank executives were being questioned over suspected violation of the Commercial Code but gave no other details.

The bank's president, Katsuhiko Kondo, appearing before a committee of the Upper House of parliament on Thursday, said he was unaware of prosecutors' questioning of DKB executives on suspected violation of the commercial code.
"If it is true (that prosecutors are questioning the bank officials), it is regrettable," Kondo told the committee.

Last Friday, top executives of DKB, including Kondo and chairman Kuniji Miyazaki, announced their resignations, effective from June, to take responsibility for the bank's involvement in improper loans to a client linked to an alleged racketeer, Ryuichi Koike.
DKB said on May 23 it had provided a total of 26 billion yen in cumulative loans to a company linked to Koike and his younger brother, Yoshinori.
It also said the bank may have covered up details of the loans to the Koikes ahead of Ministry of Finance inspections in 1990 and 1994.
Both Ryuichi and Yoshinori Koike were arrested in May on suspicion of violating Japan's commercial code by taking some 50 million yen in illegal payments from Nomura Securities Co Ltd.

Earlier this month, Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Council (SESC), sought legal action against Nomura by filing a criminal complaint with prosecutors against the firm, two former Nomura executives and a company official, alleging that they compensated a client linked to Koike for investment losses.
Kyodo news agency reported on Thursday that prosecutors are questioning four executives of DKB.
